<!-- Generated by `make docs-generate` (ocidex-cli gen-reference). Do not edit by hand. -->

Command-line client for OCIDex.

Commands are noun then verb: `ocidex-cli sbom push`, `ocidex-cli registry list`.

Configuration is resolved in this order, most specific first: command-line flag,
environment variable, ~/.config/ocidex/config.yaml, built-in default. The API key
is deliberately not a flag — see docs/adr/0029-cli-design.md.

## Global flags

Every command accepts these.

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-o`, `--output` |  | output format: table, json, or yaml (config output, default table) |
| `--server` |  | OCIDex base URL (env OCIDEX_URL, config server, default `http://localhost:8080`) |

## ocidex-cli artifact

Work with tracked artifacts

### ocidex-cli artifact changelog

Show what changed between successive versions of an artifact.

An artifact usually has several SBOMs per version — one per architecture and
flavor — so a changelog only means something once that axis is pinned. Pass
--arch and --flavor when the artifact has more than one; the available values
are printed to stderr in table mode.

The history is paged, newest first: an artifact with a thousand versions has a
thousand transitions and each one carries a full component diff. Page back
through it with --offset.

```
ocidex-cli artifact changelog <id> [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--arch` |  | architecture to follow, e.g. amd64 |
| `--flavor` |  | image flavor to follow, e.g. distroless |
| `--limit` | `0` | maximum transitions to return (server default 20) |
| `--offset` | `0` | transitions to skip, counting back from the newest |
| `--subject-version` |  | compare only within this version |

### ocidex-cli artifact get

Show one artifact in full

```
ocidex-cli artifact get <id>
```

### ocidex-cli artifact license-summary

Count components by license across an artifact's latest SBOM

```
ocidex-cli artifact license-summary <id>
```

### ocidex-cli artifact list

List tracked artifacts.

The SBOMS column reads sufficient/total: the server hides artifacts with no
sufficiently enriched SBOM unless --include-insufficient is given.

```
ocidex-cli artifact list [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--include-insufficient` |  | also list artifacts whose SBOMs are not sufficiently enriched |
| `--limit` | `0` | maximum artifacts to return (server default 50) |
| `--name` |  | filter by artifact name |
| `--offset` | `0` | index of the first artifact to return |
| `--type` |  | filter by CycloneDX type, e.g. container or application |

## ocidex-cli component

Search the packages found inside SBOMs.

There are two views of the same data, because the server offers two and they
answer different questions. `list` is deduplicated: one row per distinct
package, with the number of SBOMs it appears in — use it to browse. `search`
is per-occurrence: one row per SBOM a named package appears in, with the version
that SBOM carries — use it to answer "who ships the vulnerable version".

### ocidex-cli component get

Show one package occurrence in full.

The id is a component id from `component search`, which identifies the
package inside one SBOM — hashes, licenses, and external references are all
that SBOM's view of it.

```
ocidex-cli component get <id>
```

### ocidex-cli component list

Browse distinct packages across every visible SBOM.

One row per distinct package, not per occurrence: VERSIONS and SBOMS say how
many of each are behind it. Run `component purl-types` for the values
--purl-type accepts.

```
ocidex-cli component list [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--group` |  | filter by package group, e.g. a Maven groupId |
| `--limit` | `0` | maximum packages to return (server default 50) |
| `--name` |  | filter by package name (substring match) |
| `--offset` | `0` | index of the first package to return |
| `--purl-type` |  | filter by purl type, e.g. golang, npm, deb |
| `--sort` |  | sort field (server default: name) |
| `--sort-dir` |  | sort direction: asc or desc |
| `--type` |  | filter by CycloneDX component type, e.g. library |

### ocidex-cli component purl-types

List the purl types present in visible SBOMs.

These are the values `component list --purl-type` accepts; they depend
on what has actually been ingested, not on a fixed vocabulary.

```
ocidex-cli component purl-types
```

### ocidex-cli component search

Find every SBOM a named package appears in.

One row per occurrence, so the same package appears once per SBOM that carries
it, with that SBOM's version. The name is matched by the server, not globbed
here.

```
ocidex-cli component search <name> [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--group` |  | filter by package group, e.g. a Maven groupId |
| `--limit` | `0` | maximum occurrences to return (server default 50) |
| `--offset` | `0` | index of the first occurrence to return |
| `--version` |  | filter to one version |

### ocidex-cli component versions

Show which version of a package each artifact carries.

This is the drift question: one row per artifact shipping the named package,
with the version it has. Unpaginated — the server returns the whole set.

```
ocidex-cli component versions <name> [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--group` |  | filter by package group, e.g. a Maven groupId |
| `--type` |  | filter by CycloneDX component type, e.g. library |
| `--version` |  | filter to one version |

## ocidex-cli job

Inspect the registry scan queue.

A job is one attempt to pull an image and catalog it. Jobs are created by the
scanner, not by this CLI; what you can do here is watch them and, as an admin,
put a failed one back in the queue.

### ocidex-cli job get

Show one scan job in full.

The fields that matter on a failure are LAST ERROR and ATTEMPTS: the queue
retries on its own, so a job with several attempts and a stable error is stuck
rather than merely slow.

```
ocidex-cli job get <id>
```

### ocidex-cli job list

List scan jobs, newest first.

Without --state this lists every state, including the succeeded jobs that make
up most of the queue's history. --state failed is the one worth watching.

```
ocidex-cli job list [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--limit` | `0` | maximum jobs to return (server default 50) |
| `--offset` | `0` | index of the first job to return |
| `--state` |  | filter by state: queued, running, succeeded, or failed |

### ocidex-cli job retry

Put a failed scan job back in the queue.

Admin-only. The server returns no body, so success is silent; re-run
`job get &lt;id&gt;` to see the job back in the queued state.

```
ocidex-cli job retry <id>
```

## ocidex-cli key

Manage your API keys.

Every subcommand here needs an existing key, so the first one has to come from
the web UI. After that a key can mint its successors.

### ocidex-cli key create

Create an API key.

The key is printed once, on stdout, and never again. Everything else this
command says goes to stderr, so `ocidex-cli key create --name ci &gt; key.txt`
captures exactly the key and nothing else.

Capabilities are a ceiling, not a grant: the key can never do more than your
namespace roles allow, and a role change narrows every key you hold without any
key change. Omitting --capability asks for all of them, which resolves to
exactly what you can do. Name them where something narrower will do: a key that
only ingests cannot delete an SBOM even where you can.

```
ocidex-cli key create [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--capability` |  | capability this key may exercise, repeatable (default: all of them) |
| `--name` |  | human-readable label for the key (required) |

### ocidex-cli key delete

Revoke an API key.

Takes the key's UUID, which `key list` shows — not the key itself, which
you are not expected to still have.

```
ocidex-cli key delete <id>
```

### ocidex-cli key list

List your API keys.

Only metadata: the key itself is stored hashed and cannot be shown again. PREFIX
is what identifies a key in the audit log.

```
ocidex-cli key list
```

## ocidex-cli login

Save a server URL and API key to the config file.

Prompts for whatever is not given as a flag, verifies the key by asking the
server who you are, and only then writes `~/.config/ocidex/config.yaml` with
mode 0600. A key that does not work is rejected here rather than at the next
command.

--key exists for non-interactive setup, but prefer OCIDEX_API_KEY in CI: an
argument is visible in the process table and in most runners' command logs.

```
ocidex-cli login [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--key` |  | API key (prompted when omitted; prefer OCIDEX_API_KEY in CI) |
| `--server-url` |  | server to log in to (prompted when omitted) |

## ocidex-cli logout

Remove the stored API key.

Only the key: the server URL and output preference are settings, not
credentials, and re-typing them after every logout is friction with no security
benefit. The file is deleted outright once nothing is left in it.

This does not revoke the key server-side — use `key delete &lt;id&gt;` for that.

```
ocidex-cli logout
```

## ocidex-cli namespace

Manage namespaces.

A namespace owns sources and everything ingested through them, and its
visibility governs who can read those artifacts (ADR-039).

Every command that takes a namespace accepts either its UUID or its name; a
name is resolved through /api/v1/namespaces/by-name before the call.

### ocidex-cli namespace create

Create a namespace.

Visibility defaults to private, so a namespace created without --visibility is
readable only by its owner.

  ocidex-cli namespace create --name acme --visibility public

```
ocidex-cli namespace create [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--name` |  | namespace name, unique across the server |
| `--visibility` |  | who can read artifacts under it: public or private (default private) |

### ocidex-cli namespace delete

Delete a namespace and everything ingested under it

```
ocidex-cli namespace delete <id|name> [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-y`, `--yes` |  | do not prompt for confirmation |

### ocidex-cli namespace get

Show one namespace in full

```
ocidex-cli namespace get <id|name>
```

### ocidex-cli namespace list

List visible namespaces

```
ocidex-cli namespace list
```

### ocidex-cli namespace update

Rename a namespace or change its visibility.

Both fields are omit-to-keep on the API's PATCH, so only the flags actually
given are sent — no read-modify-write, and nothing else can be reset by
accident.

```
ocidex-cli namespace update <id|name> [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--name` |  | new namespace name |
| `--visibility` |  | new visibility: public or private |

## ocidex-cli registry

Manage OCI registry sources.

Every command that takes a registry accepts either its UUID or its name; a name
is resolved through /api/v1/registries/by-name before the call.

### ocidex-cli registry create

Register an OCI registry to scan.

Omitting --namespace gives the registry a namespace of its own, named after it.
Pass an existing namespace to put several sources under one owner and one
visibility setting.

```
ocidex-cli registry create [flags]
```

Examples:

```sh
  ocidex-cli registry create --name ghcr --url ghcr.io --type ghcr \
    --namespace myorg --tag-pattern semver --auth-token-file ./ghcr.pat
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--auth-token-file` |  | file holding the registry token or PAT |
| `--auth-username` |  | registry username; omit for anonymous access |
| `--include-untagged` |  | scan untagged manifests (zot, harbor, ghcr) |
| `--insecure` |  | allow HTTP (non-TLS) connections |
| `--max-tag-age-days` | `0` | skip tags whose image is older than this; needs created order, 0 = no limit |
| `--name` |  | human-readable registry name (required) |
| `--namespace` |  | namespace to create the registry in, created on first use |
| `--poll-interval-minutes` | `0` | minutes between polls |
| `--repository` |  | explicit repository to walk; repeatable, bypasses catalog discovery |
| `--repository-pattern` |  | glob for repositories to ingest; repeatable, empty = all |
| `--scan-mode` |  | scanning mode |
| `--tag-limit` | `0` | newest tags kept per repository; 0 = unlimited (server default 50) |
| `--tag-order` |  | how newest is decided: auto, semver, created, or lexical |
| `--tag-pattern` |  | glob or 'semver' for tags to ingest; repeatable, empty = all |
| `--trust-identity` |  | regex matched against the Fulcio certificate SAN (keyless) |
| `--trust-issuer` |  | expected OIDC issuer URL (keyless) |
| `--trust-public-key-file` |  | file holding the PEM-encoded EC public key (public_key) |
| `--type` |  | registry type, e.g. ghcr, zot, harbor, docker |
| `--url` |  | registry address, e.g. ghcr.io |
| `--verification-mode` |  | signature verification: none, public_key, or keyless |
| `--visibility` |  | public or private |
| `--webhook-secret-file` |  | file holding the bearer token required on incoming webhooks |

### ocidex-cli registry delete

Delete a registry and everything ingested from it

```
ocidex-cli registry delete <id|name> [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-y`, `--yes` |  | do not prompt for confirmation |

### ocidex-cli registry get

Show one registry in full

```
ocidex-cli registry get <id|name>
```

### ocidex-cli registry list

List visible registries

```
ocidex-cli registry list [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--limit` | `0` | maximum registries to return (server default 50) |
| `--offset` | `0` | index of the first registry to return |

### ocidex-cli registry preview

Show what a registry would scan, without scanning (ADR-0053).

With a registry, previews its saved configuration and credentials. Without one,
previews the configuration given by the same flags as create, before it is
saved. Either way nothing is queued. The table has one row per repository; the
total estimate goes to stderr.

```
ocidex-cli registry preview [id|name] [flags]
```

Examples:

```sh
  ocidex-cli registry preview ghcr
  ocidex-cli registry preview --url quay.io --type docker \
    --repository metallb/controller --tag-pattern semver --tag-limit 5
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--auth-token-file` |  | file holding the registry token or PAT |
| `--auth-username` |  | registry username; omit for anonymous access |
| `--include-untagged` |  | scan untagged manifests (zot, harbor, ghcr) |
| `--insecure` |  | allow HTTP (non-TLS) connections |
| `--max-tag-age-days` | `0` | skip tags whose image is older than this; needs created order, 0 = no limit |
| `--poll-interval-minutes` | `0` | minutes between polls |
| `--repository` |  | explicit repository to walk; repeatable, bypasses catalog discovery |
| `--repository-pattern` |  | glob for repositories to ingest; repeatable, empty = all |
| `--scan-mode` |  | scanning mode |
| `--tag-limit` | `0` | newest tags kept per repository; 0 = unlimited (server default 50) |
| `--tag-order` |  | how newest is decided: auto, semver, created, or lexical |
| `--tag-pattern` |  | glob or 'semver' for tags to ingest; repeatable, empty = all |
| `--trust-identity` |  | regex matched against the Fulcio certificate SAN (keyless) |
| `--trust-issuer` |  | expected OIDC issuer URL (keyless) |
| `--trust-public-key-file` |  | file holding the PEM-encoded EC public key (public_key) |
| `--type` |  | registry type, e.g. ghcr, zot, harbor, docker |
| `--url` |  | registry address, e.g. ghcr.io |
| `--verification-mode` |  | signature verification: none, public_key, or keyless |
| `--visibility` |  | public or private |

### ocidex-cli registry scan

Trigger an ad-hoc scan

```
ocidex-cli registry scan <id|name>
```

### ocidex-cli registry update

Change a registry's configuration.

Only the flags you pass are changed: the current registry is read first and the
given flags applied to it, because the API's PATCH body is a whole registry.

```
ocidex-cli registry update <id|name> [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--auth-token-file` |  | file holding the registry token or PAT |
| `--auth-username` |  | registry username; omit for anonymous access |
| `--enabled` | `true` | whether OCIDex polls this registry |
| `--include-untagged` |  | scan untagged manifests (zot, harbor, ghcr) |
| `--insecure` |  | allow HTTP (non-TLS) connections |
| `--max-tag-age-days` | `0` | skip tags whose image is older than this; needs created order, 0 = no limit |
| `--name` |  | rename the registry |
| `--poll-interval-minutes` | `0` | minutes between polls |
| `--repository` |  | explicit repository to walk; repeatable, bypasses catalog discovery |
| `--repository-pattern` |  | glob for repositories to ingest; repeatable, empty = all |
| `--scan-mode` |  | scanning mode |
| `--tag-limit` | `0` | newest tags kept per repository; 0 = unlimited (server default 50) |
| `--tag-order` |  | how newest is decided: auto, semver, created, or lexical |
| `--tag-pattern` |  | glob or 'semver' for tags to ingest; repeatable, empty = all |
| `--trust-identity` |  | regex matched against the Fulcio certificate SAN (keyless) |
| `--trust-issuer` |  | expected OIDC issuer URL (keyless) |
| `--trust-public-key-file` |  | file holding the PEM-encoded EC public key (public_key) |
| `--type` |  | registry type, e.g. ghcr, zot, harbor, docker |

## ocidex-cli sbom

Work with SBOMs

### ocidex-cli sbom delete

Delete a SBOM

```
ocidex-cli sbom delete <id> [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-y`, `--yes` |  | delete without confirming |

### ocidex-cli sbom diff

Show what changed between two SBOMs.

In table mode the change list goes to stdout and the tally to stderr, so the
table survives a pipe. -o json and -o yaml emit the whole changelog entry,
including the two SBOM references and the summary.

```
ocidex-cli sbom diff --from <id> --to <id> [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--from` |  | SBOM to compare from (required) |
| `--to` |  | SBOM to compare to (required) |

### ocidex-cli sbom diff-tree

Show what changed between two SBOMs, as a dependency tree.

The tree is the server's: roots, direct/transitive placement, and the per-node
descendant change counts are all computed there (ADR-021), so this renders and
does not recompute. A node is marked +, -, or ~ for added, removed, or changed,
and a node with unchanged descendants that themselves changed is annotated with
the counts underneath it.

```
ocidex-cli sbom diff-tree --from <id> --to <id> [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--changed-only` |  | prune branches with no change anywhere beneath them |
| `--from` |  | SBOM to compare from (required) |
| `--to` |  | SBOM to compare to (required) |

### ocidex-cli sbom get

Show one SBOM in full

```
ocidex-cli sbom get <id> [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--raw` |  | print the stored CycloneDX document instead of OCIDex's summary |

### ocidex-cli sbom list

List visible SBOMs.

--serial-number identifies one document; --digest identifies one subject, so it
returns every SBOM recorded for that image or artifact.

```
ocidex-cli sbom list [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--digest` |  | return only SBOMs whose subject has this digest |
| `--limit` | `0` | maximum SBOMs to return (server default 50) |
| `--offset` | `0` | index of the first SBOM to return |
| `--serial-number` |  | return only the SBOM with this CycloneDX serial number |

### ocidex-cli sbom push

Upload a CycloneDX SBOM for a build artifact.

The SBOM lands in the namespace that owns --source. For a non-container subject
the server requires the subject to be declared rather than inferred, because a
`syft dir:` scan describes the directory it scanned, not the thing you built.

Authentication is via the OCIDEX_API_KEY environment variable, or the api-key
key in ~/.config/ocidex/config.yaml.

```
ocidex-cli sbom push <sbom-file> [flags]
```

Examples:

```sh
  ocidex-cli sbom push ./ocidex.cdx.json \
    --source myorg/ci \
    --artifact-file ./bin/ocidex \
    --subject-type application \
    --subject-name ocidex \
    --subject-purl pkg:golang/github.com/pfenerty/ocidex@v1.2.3 \
    --version v1.2.3 \
    --arch amd64
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--arch` |  | architecture the artifact was built for, e.g. amd64 |
| `--arch-file` |  | read --arch from this file |
| `--artifact-file` |  | artifact the SBOM describes; its sha256 becomes the digest |
| `--digest` |  | artifact digest, if it is already known (mutually exclusive with --artifact-file) |
| `--source` |  | ingest source: UUID or &lt;namespace&gt;/&lt;name&gt; (required) |
| `--subject-group` |  | subject group, e.g. github.com/pfenerty |
| `--subject-name` |  | subject name, e.g. ocidex |
| `--subject-purl` |  | subject package URL |
| `--subject-type` |  | CycloneDX component type, e.g. application |
| `--version` |  | subject version, e.g. v1.2.3 |
| `--version-file` |  | read --version from this file |

## ocidex-cli source

Manage ingest sources.

A source is one ingest channel into a namespace (ADR-039). `create` makes an
upload source, the kind SBOMs are pushed to directly; an OCI registry source is
created with `ocidex-cli registry create`, which configures the registry behind
it at the same time.

Sources are named uniquely only within their namespace, so the API offers no
by-name lookup for them: these commands take a source UUID, which
`ocidex-cli source list` prints.

### ocidex-cli source create

Create an upload source in a namespace.

An upload source has nothing to configure: it is the channel SBOMs pushed with
`ocidex-cli sbom push` are attributed to.

  ocidex-cli source create --name ci-uploads --namespace acme

```
ocidex-cli source create [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--name` |  | source name, unique within the namespace |
| `--namespace` |  | owning namespace, by id or name |

### ocidex-cli source delete

Delete a source and everything ingested through it

```
ocidex-cli source delete <id> [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-y`, `--yes` |  | do not prompt for confirmation |

### ocidex-cli source get

Show one source in full

```
ocidex-cli source get <id>
```

### ocidex-cli source list

List visible sources

```
ocidex-cli source list [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--namespace` |  | only sources in this namespace, by id or name |

### ocidex-cli source update

Rename a source.

The name is all a source owns; its namespace and kind are fixed at creation, so
moving a source between namespaces means creating a new one.

```
ocidex-cli source update <id> [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--name` |  | new source name |

## ocidex-cli version

Print the CLI version, commit, and build date

```
ocidex-cli version
```
